text:
The future of artificial intelligence is a topic of intense debate. Many experts predict we will move beyond today’s specialized systems to achieve Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI. This would be a machine with human-like cognitive abilities, able to learn and reason across any task.

The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could solve complex problems in medicine, climate change, and science. However, the risks are equally significant, such as job displacement or the challenge of controlling a super-intelligent system.

Timeline predictions vary widely. Some optimists believe AGI is only a decade away, while cautious researchers suggest it could take fifty years or more. Ultimately, how we manage this powerful technology will determine if it becomes our greatest tool or our biggest challenge.
